Welcome to 404 Ideas

We are a passionate team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge under the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. Our mission is to leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) and smart software solutions to monitor astronauts' vital health data
summary:
AstroVitals is an interactive, AI-assisted astronaut health-monitoring prototype developed by Team 404 Ideas for long-duration space missions.

Our platform combines an interactive 3D astronaut digital twin, physiological data visualization, experimental heart-rate forecasting, and NASA-based scientific research within an immersive mission-control environment.

Using real terrestrial physiological recordings from PhysioNet BIDMC, AstroVitals analyzes heart rate, pulse rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation. Experimental forecasting models include Ridge Regression, a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and IBM Granite TinyTimeMixer R2.1.

The platform also integrates historical NASA DONKI space-weather data, simulated communication blackouts, an interactive mission timeline, and AURA, a rule-based mission health guide.

Our goal is to explore how local AI inference, interactive visualization, and evidence-based research could improve future astronaut health-monitoring systems when communication with Earth is delayed.

AstroVitals is currently a functional, browser-based research prototype. It distinguishes recorded medical data from simulated astronaut scenarios and does not claim to provide validated medical diagnoses or autonomous treatment.
details:
AstroVitals: Autonomous Health Monitoring Research Prototype

The Challenge

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to unique health risks, including cardiovascular changes, bone-density reduction, fluid redistribution, fatigue, and communication delays.

During deep-space exploration, communication with Earth can take several minutes, making immediate ground-based medical guidance difficult.

Our challenge was to explore how astronauts could monitor physiological conditions, investigate potential health changes, and access understandable information using locally executable software.

Our Solution

Team 404 Ideas developed AstroVitals, an interactive, browser-based astronaut health-monitoring and bio-digital-twin prototype.

The platform combines real physiological datasets, experimental AI forecasting, interactive 3D visualizations, NASA scientific resources, and simulated mission-health scenarios.

Its core components include:

1. Physiological Monitoring Workspace

AstroVitals visualizes heart rate, pulse rate, respiratory rate, and blood oxygen saturation using actual terrestrial recordings from the PhysioNet BIDMC dataset.

Our data-preparation pipeline processed 53 recordings from 46 patients, containing 25,493 numerical samples.

The recordings were divided into patient-separated training, validation, and testing groups to support reproducible experiments.

Users can explore recorded measurements, inspect missing values, and examine explicitly simulated signal-dropout scenarios.

2. Experimental AI Health Forecasting

We implemented several experimental forecasting methods:

  • Persistence: predicts the latest recorded heart-rate value.
  • Ridge Regression: a trained linear forecasting model.
  • Multilayer Perceptron (MLP): a compact trained neural network.
  • Ridge/MLP Blend: combines 20% Ridge and 80% MLP predictions.
  • IBM Granite TinyTimeMixer R2.1: a pretrained time-series foundation model.

The application generates experimental 10-second heart-rate predictions.

Granite executes through ONNX Runtime Web and WebAssembly, allowing model inference inside the browser.

We also evaluated the trained models on 40 independent VitalDB surgical cases containing 185,152 observed targets.

In our recorded benchmark, the persistence baseline achieved a mean absolute error of 1.449 beats/min, while the Ridge/MLP blend achieved a root mean squared error of 3.873 beats/min.

These results are preliminary engineering benchmarks using Earth-based measurements, not astronaut-specific clinical validation.

3. Interactive 3D Astronaut Digital Twin

The system provides an interactive 3D astronaut and anatomical visualization environment powered by Three.js and WebGL.

It presents animated organs, cardiovascular concepts, and simulated physiological changes during long-duration missions.

Users can explore mission-health concepts through visual interaction rather than relying exclusively on numerical dashboards.

4. AURA Mission Health Guide

AURA is an interactive, rule-based mission guide that provides predefined explanations of simulated crew-health conditions.

It allows users to investigate cardiovascular changes, skeletal health, fluid shifts, and mission countermeasure scenarios.

AURA currently operates using keyword-based responses and programmed logic rather than a live generative medical language model.

5. Mission Simulation and Communication Blackouts

AstroVitals includes interactive mission-day scenarios, simulated communication blackouts, and illustrative health countermeasure demonstrations.

These features explore how local software could remain useful when communication with Earth is delayed.

Countermeasure effects are simulated and do not represent medically validated treatment outcomes.

6. NASA Space-Weather Data Integration

We integrated historical NASA DONKI geomagnetic-storm observations from May 2024 into the interactive planetary exploration environment.

The application displays recorded event timestamps and planetary Kp indices.

These observations provide Earth space-weather context and are not presented as direct measurements of astronaut radiation exposure.

NASA Scientific Foundation

The project references NASA's Open Science Data Repository, including Inspiration4 study OSD-575, as well as NASA's Human Research Program, Human Research Roadmap, evidence reports, and NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1.

These resources informed our exploration of cardiovascular adaptation, bone health, Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), and crew-health requirements.

NASA research references are distinguished from the terrestrial recordings used for model training.

Development Technologies

Frontend: React 19, JavaScript, JSX, HTML5, CSS, Tailwind CSS 4, React Router 7, Vite 6, Framer Motion, and Lucide React.

3D Visualization: Three.js, WebGL, glTF/GLB assets, GLTFLoader, DRACOLoader, and OrbitControls.

Data Processing: Python 3, CSV, JSON, dataset-version tracking, SHA-256 source verification, and patient-separated dataset preparation.

AI and Machine Learning: Ridge Regression, Multilayer Perceptron, IBM Granite TinyTimeMixer R2.1, ONNX Runtime Web, and WebAssembly.

Audio: Native Web Audio API for procedurally synthesized space ambience, notifications, alarms, and interaction sounds.

Development and Deployment: Git, GitHub, Node.js, npm, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, and Vercel-compatible static builds.

The prototype runs in a compatible desktop or mobile browser. No physical astronaut sensors or medical monitoring hardware are connected.

Creativity and Innovation

AstroVitals brings together experimental health forecasting, recorded physiological data, mission simulations, interactive anatomical visualization, and NASA space-weather observations in one accessible interface.

Its design emphasizes explainability, transparency, and the potential for browser-based local AI inference.

Our approach separates recorded biomedical observations, experimental forecasts, simulated astronaut conditions, and NASA scientific references.

Intended Impact

AstroVitals explores a foundation for future astronaut health-monitoring tools that could support early investigation of physiological changes, interactive health education, and decision-support research.

Potential future improvements include real wearable-sensor integration, astronaut-specific model validation, enhanced anomaly detection, and evaluation under actual spaceflight operational constraints.

The current application is a functional research and educational proof of concept, not an approved medical diagnostic or treatment system.

Super Intelligence Transparency

OpenAI ChatGPT assisted our research discussions, technical planning, documentation, and development iterations. Team 404 Ideas remained responsible for the project's design, integration, implementation, and validation.

The implemented forecasting models, scripted mission guide, and simulation rules are documented separately to distinguish actual machine-learning inference from deterministic demonstrations.
